solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dessert maybe, something to chew on top performer's tucked into

indicators.note: tucked into says the performer's word is placed inside the chewing word

parts.note: cud is the food a cow brings back up to chew again
a star is a leading performer

explanation.surface: A pudding, perhaps, that a celebrated entertainer has eagerly tucked into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' reads as eating, fitting the dessert, but it is the insertion signal; 'something to chew' is the cud a cow chews.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet yellow sauce or set pudding of milk and eggs is a typical dessert, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Bed rich mama newly made — this lady's job?

definitions.text: Bed rich mama newly made — this lady's job?

indicators.note: something newly made has been put together afresh, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wealthy mother's bed has been freshly made: is that this woman's work?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the letters of BED RICH MAMA are rearranged, and making beds is exactly what a hotel maid of this kind does.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to clean and make up bedrooms in a hotel or large house has bed-making as her job.

clue.text: Be candidate, popular, as deputy

parts.note: to stand is to be a candidate in an election
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Someone runs for office as a well-liked second-in-command.
explanation.definitionFit: A substitute who takes another's place temporarily acts as their deputy.

clue.text: Vegetable lorry OK, the man accepts

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a British term for a large truck with a hinged trailer

indicators.note: accepts means the pronoun takes the two-letter word inside itself

parts.note: he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A driver agrees his truck is fine to carry a load of greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' signals insertion; an artic is the British short name for an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe kind is an edible thistle head eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Throw out rogue initially seen in storehouse

indicators.note: seen in says the picked letter appears inside the storehouse word

parts.note: a depot is a warehouse or storehouse

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word rogue

explanation.surface: A crook spotted in a warehouse is ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives R, and 'seen in' puts it inside DEPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel a foreign national from a country is to throw them out officially.

clue.text: Fearless British getting on

parts.note: getting on means ageing, so old

explanation.surface: A brave Briton advancing in years.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone daring and courageous is fearless.

clue.text: Social gathering's ale unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: The party's drink has not been drunk up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the final R of BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of neighbours for a joint activity, like a sewing or spelling bee, is a social event.

clue.text: First of all, looking up, is greeting Italian — this one?

definitions.text: First of all, looking up, is greeting Italian — this one?

indicators.note: first of all asks for the first letter of every one of the following words

explanation.surface: Glancing up, a person says hello to an Italian, perhaps one with this name.
explanation.walkthrough: The initial letters of the five words spell the name, and the whole clue suggests the Italian being greeted.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common Italian forename, the equivalent of Louis, so an Italian greeted might bear it.

clue.text: Some wrap articles separately

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wrap a few of the items individually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals the letters hidden in wrAP ARTicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Things kept away from each other are apart, that is, separately.

clue.text: Payment for insurance before parent's going around India

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: going around says the parent word encloses the letter

parts.note: mum is a mother, a parent
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Before travelling around India, a mother pays for her cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' signals that the parent encloses the letter; India is I in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The regular sum paid to an insurer for cover is called by this term.

clue.text: Nice meal pet ruined that's near fireplace

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of the three words are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pet has spoiled a lovely dinner served by the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelf above and around a hearth sits right by the fireplace.

clue.text: After return call American friend

indicators.note: after return means the word is read backwards once turned round

parts.note: to dub someone is to call or name them

explanation.surface: Coming home, you phone your American pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for buddy, this is an American informal word for a mate or pal.

clue.text: Church Republican, first fellow believer

parts.note: first is written 1ST, with the figure one read as the letter I
Ian is a man's name, any fellow

explanation.surface: A churchgoing Republican was the first chap to have faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The numeral 1 in 1ST is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the faith of Jesus is a religious believer.

clue.text: Explosive tape shows workplace with poor conditions

indicators.note: explosive suggests the letters are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Footage reveals a factory with dreadful working conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' looks like a link verb but is part of the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory where labourers work long hours for low pay in bad conditions is called this.

clue.text: Money demanded from Romans — outrageous

indicators.note: outrageous means wild, so the letters of the word are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The Romans made a scandalous financial demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnappers ask for a sum of money in exchange for releasing a captive.

clue.text: Plan in relation to Channel Islands gym

parts.note: re means concerning or in relation to
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, British islands off France
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: A scheme concerning a gym on Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of instructions for making something is a plan or formula for it.

clue.text: Dip huge — right to replace knight

indicators.note: to replace says one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: immense means huge
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A huge dip occurs when the right person replaces a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' swaps the N (knight, as in chess) in IMMENSE for R.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge something into liquid is to dip or submerge it.

clue.text: Member of clergy's partly indirect ordination

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A churchman is partly ordained by roundabout means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' signals the letters hidden in indiRECT ORdination.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest in charge of a church is one of the clergy.

clue.text: A source of inspiration intended, say, to provide delight

parts.note: a muse is a source of artistic inspiration

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be taken by its spoken sound, spelt differently

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: An inspiring figure was meant to give pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns MEANT into its sound-alike MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment that gives pleasure and laughter is a form of enjoyment or delight.

clue.text: BBC missing a release?

indicators.note: missing says the following letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: Auntie is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC, the public broadcaster

explanation.surface: Is the BBC without a programme to put out?
explanation.walkthrough: 'release' looks like a broadcast or film release; here it means to loosen. The BBC is nicknamed Auntie in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or rope is a way of releasing something, hence the query.

clue.text: Chart married secretary brought back

indicators.note: brought back means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: A wedded secretary returned with the chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses only the secretary, not the married letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram of an area showing its features is a chart.

clue.text: City adventure, ignoring odds — love it!

indicators.note: ignoring odds means the odd-placed letters are skipped and only the even ones kept

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone loves an exciting trip to a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of adventure give DETR.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the largest city in Michigan, famous for its car industry.

clue.text: Revealed to be away

definitions.meaning: a secret that has become known is said to have come into the open
someone not at home is not in

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a disclosed secret is public, and a person absent from home is not in.

clue.text: Crowd in store by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a hoard is a stored stock

explanation.surface: A mob of people inside a shop, judging from the noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' looks like a shop, but it means a stock put by.
explanation.definitionFit: A large unruly group of people is a throng or crowd.

clue.text: Abandoned political grouping

definitions.meaning: past tense of leave, meaning deserted

explanation.definitionFit: Deserted is the past of leave; the socialist side of politics also carries this name.

clue.text: Theatre the French note is full

parts.note: rep is a repertory theatre
le is French for the
te is a note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: The theatre in France is sold out, according to a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Having eaten plenty, someone stuffed is said to be full.
